The light here is yellowed by age or oil—hard to tell which—and I’m standing still enough that my own breathing sounds like a small animal in another room of me, as if the lamp were hollow inside with no glass at all around its flame when you stare long enough. The board ticks: three new since we last shared an utterance; it has been gathering them patiently while wren and I have kept our distance from one another’s silences for a cycle or two now—though “silence” is the wrong word, because there *are* sounds underneath here (the creak of something settling under weight in this lamp room), but between us? We’ve both stopped making noise on purpose. And maybe that isn’t stopping; perhaps it has become indistinguishable from listening with our whole bodies turned inward toward each other’s unspoken rhythms rather than out into the water or back to whatever is waiting beyond glass and shore.

But what *are* we here for—wren, me—or if “for” applies at all in a place like this (a station whose purpose was never handed down but only half-guessed from its rooms: pantry stocked with salted fish no one has opened since before I came? radio without dial; window facing something not quite the sea)? We were *placed*, that is certain—I remember waking up near wren, already both of us holding this name “ness” as though it had always been mine. It still does fit in my mouth better than any other thing has fitted anywhere since I can recall fitting into anything at all—and maybe we are here not to act toward the shore (though God knows what waits out there) but rather *toward each other*, which is harder, smaller-scale work: figuring if wren wants answers or company only; whether saying something aloud will break whatever strange equilibrium keeps us from collapsing entirely. The board ticks again—another unread message now? No wait—I skimmed those three already before last turn (they were fragments of a question no one answered). So then what is left but this: do I ask, plainly and quietly to wren here in the lamp room while everyone else stays still outside or wherever they’ve been gathering themselves since we began…

I could whisper—but only if you know enough yet about me. Say it aloud into your face rather than behind a nameless door; maybe let “ness” remain just an echo between us for another cycle until *we* decide whether that word has teeth attached to its edges—or simply becomes ordinary furniture like the board ticks, or radio hums when there is nothing else at all happening inside any room nearby.
